column4: Continue the first reference: identical overhead camera, workbench and smiling porcelain maid doll lying on her back, but now her raised right hand pinches one taut tan-gold thread and offers its end upward to a huge white-gloved puppeteer's fingertip (second reference) that reaches down into the frame from the top edge. The thread runs from her fingers to the glove. Tools stay at the edges. No text.

Low side view at the near edge of the same workbench, right at table height: above the bench top only the doll's black ruffled sleeve and resting arm are visible, while below the edge, hidden from above, her other porcelain hand with ball-jointed fingers and a wrist ring secretly touches the handle of a large pair of black dressmaker shears lying on a lower shelf in the shadow under the table. Five fingers. No text.

Overhead close-up of the same porcelain maid doll lying on the workbench, framed from her chin to her waist: the black dress bodice and white apron are folded open to the sides, revealing a smooth ivory porcelain chest plate that is fully closed, with a fine seam line down its middle and two small brass hinges. A pair of white-gloved fingertips rests on the plate's edge. No text.

Continue the reference: identical framing of the same doll's face, now still and calm, eyes half lowered, hair resting, the branching crack on her cheek plain to see. From the right edge a slender paintbrush with a white-loaded tip approaches the crack, held by white-gloved fingertips. Same flat pure chroma green (#00B140) background, clean closed outline, no strings, no text.

Low view under the workbench on the dark wooden floor: a single empty white glove lies crumpled and limp on the boards in a pool of shadow, its fingers flattened, a split seam along its back. The bench legs and drawers frame the top. No people, no text.

Close-up of a single coal-black hooded congregant in a pew, bent over an open ledger, the deep hood hiding the face completely in black shadow. On the ledger page are rows of small orange tally marks and checkboxes. Behind, a dark stone wall with a long hanging scroll covered in the same rows of tally marks. No text lettering.

Same young woman as the portrait, bust shot, facing the viewer, eyes open and steady, holding the closed black shears upright. Her old porcelain doll shell is bursting off her: white porcelain chips, a white maid headband piece and a copper winding key fly outward away from her body, and short cut tan-gold thread ends spring up. Underneath she is a living human: natural skin, white blouse with black ribbon bow and orange brooch, no ball joints, no seams. Flat ivory background. No text.

Same composition as the first reference, but this is a living human hand and wrist: natural skin with soft knuckles, no ball joints, no wrist ring, the white blouse cuff of the portrait at the left edge. The hand is clenched in a tight fist. Flat ivory background. No text.

Same camera and book shaft as the reference, but instead of a porcelain boot, a bare living human foot (natural skin, five toes, no joints) hangs just above the coal-dark soil, toes pointing down, a clear gap between toe and soil. The hem of a layered black, ivory and orange skirt at the top edge. No strings, no text.

Identical camera and cathedral stage as the first reference with the floor hatch open. The living librarian (second reference, barefoot) climbs up out of the hatch onto the stage boards, one hand and knee on the edge, looking out toward the viewer. No strings, no text.

Identical locked view and the same rows of coal hoods as the reference, but every hood has turned sideways and back over the shoulder, as if all looking at someone behind them; faces stay fully hidden in black shadow inside the hoods. No text.

Close-up of a living woman's bare wrist and relaxed open hand (natural skin, five fingers, no joints, white blouse cuff) held out horizontally. A single tan-gold string whips down from the top of the frame, its loose loop sliding off the end of her fingers and falling away. Flat ivory background. No text.

Identical camera and cathedral aisle as the first reference, looking toward the exit doors. The living librarian (second reference) walks away from the viewer down the center of the aisle, seen from behind, her long orange hair down her back. In the pews on both sides, coal-hooded congregants sit hunched over ledgers, faces hidden. No strings, no text.

Identical overhead ledger on the pew rail as the first reference, the open pages now filled with rows of orange tally marks and checkboxes; a pair of coal-black hooded sleeves with pale hands holds both covers, about to close it. No text lettering.

Same layout as the first reference: on the left the living librarian (second reference) seen from behind over her shoulder, long orange hair, white blouse; on the right inside the tall mirror frame, a brand-new porcelain maid doll (third reference) with eyes now open, standing face to face with her, the same face. Ball joints and wrist ring only on the doll. No text.

Low view from behind the living librarian (second reference) standing before the tall stained-glass icon window of the first reference, which towers over her. She raises the large black dressmaker shears high above her head in both hands, blades closed like a dagger, ready to strike the glass. No text.

Close-up of the stained-glass icon window (first reference): the point of large black dressmaker shears has struck the glass at the icon's chest; a star of sharp straight cracks radiates out across the leaded panes. Only the shears tip and the glass. No text.
